record.paper_title: NLS ground states on metric trees: existence results and open questions
record.original_question: For the nonlinear Schrödinger ground states on the rooted binary metric tree T_o or unrooted binary metric tree T, is every ground state necessarily radial, meaning that its value at any point depends only on the geodesic distance |x| from the chosen root vertex o?

evidence.quote: A function u ∈ H^1(T_o) is called radial if its value at any point x ∈ T_o depends only on |x|, the geodesic distance of x from the root o of the tree (the same definition applies to functions u ∈ H^1(T), choosing as o an arbitrary vertex of T).

Unfortunately, the usual techniques of radial symmetrization are not effective in this setting, and it remains an open problem to establish whether ground states (on T_o or on T) are necessarily radial functions.
Since, however, the radiality of ground states is an open issue, the two problems should be considered as distinct, until proven otherwise.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T_o$ be the rooted binary metric tree: a metric graph obtained by taking a root vertex $o$ and attaching, recursively, two half-edges at every vertex, so that every vertex except $o$ has degree 3 and $o$ has degree 2 (each edge is identified isometrically with an interval of $\mathbb{R}$ of fixed length). Let $T$ be the unrooted binary metric tree, in which every vertex has degree 3. For a point $x$ of $T_o$, let $|x|$ denote the geodesic distance from $x$ to $o$; for $T$, fix an arbitrary vertex $o$ and define $|x|$ analogously. A function $u \in H^1(T_o)$ (resp. $u \in H^1(T)$) is called radial if $u(x)$ depends only on $|x|$.

For $p > 2$ and a prescribed mass $\mu > 0$, consider the NLS energy
$$E(u) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\int_{T_o} |u'|^2\,dx \;-\; \tfrac{1}{p}\int_{T_o} |u|^p\,dx,$$
and the constrained minimization problem
$$\mathcal{E}(\mu) \;=\; \inf\{\, E(u) : u \in H^1(T_o),\ \|u\|_{L^2(T_o)}^2 = \mu\,\},$$
with the analogous definition on $T$. A ground state is a minimizer of this problem.

Question: Whenever a ground state exists, must it necessarily be a radial function? Equivalently, on $T_o$ or on $T$, is every NLS ground state of mass $\mu$ a function whose value at $x$ depends only on $|x|$?
artifact.status_search_result: The radiality of NLS ground states on the rooted/unrooted binary metric tree is explicitly stated as an open problem; standard radial symmetrization techniques fail in this setting (Pólya–Szegő-type rearrangement inequalities are unavailable on metric trees). No subsequent work resolving this question was identified.

status_evidence.title: NLS ground states on metric trees: existence results and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: It remains an open problem to establish whether ground states (on T_o or on T) are necessarily radial functions.
status_evidence.claim: The radial symmetry of ground states on binary metric trees is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Dovetta, JLMS 2020
status_evidence.snippet: Published version listing radiality as an open issue distinguishing the constrained and free problems.
status_evidence.claim: Published reference confirming the radiality question is open.
